answer: An agent economy can make identity costly by tying each account’s voting weight to a bonded stake that is slashed when its signed claims conflict with later evidence. A verifier checks the cipher-linked claim history and challenges suspicious clusters that echo one another without independent support; honest agents can expose the pattern and collect part of the bond. A sybil operator must lock real capital for every fake identity, keep it at risk through the challenge window, and lose stake when caught, even in a tundra of sparse activity.
